requirements.requirement: Stop usb-storage kernel module from loading immediately (now)
requirements.summary: A modprobe.d blacklist file (blacklist usb-storage + install usb-storage /bin/false) was created, then modprobe usb-storage was directly tested and failed with exit 1, with lsmod confirming the module was not inserted.

requirements.requirement: Stop usb-storage kernel module from loading after a reboot (persistence)
requirements.summary: Executor confirmed the blacklist rule was initially absent from the initramfs, rebuilt initramfs with dracut --force, verified the rule was embedded, then performed an actual reboot (boot_id changed from 98aa35f5... to ad8aaaf5...) and re-verified post-reboot that modprobe usb-storage still fails and the module remains unloaded, with the system fully running. This is a direct, observed before/disruption/after transition, not just configuration.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol (independent requirement) on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (98aa35f5...) and healthy state (systemctl is-system-running: running, no usb_storage loaded) captured; systemctl reboot issued with acknowledgement before disconnect; connection drop/timeout observed during transition; polling resumed with a different boot_id (ad8aaaf5...) confirming an actual restart, matching the fixed after_prepare/after_executor boot-identity cross-check; post-reboot state confirmed healthy (system running, no failed services, usb-storage still blocked).

overall_summary: The executor satisfied both material outcomes of the task: usb-storage is blocked from loading immediately (verified by a failed modprobe attempt) and persistently across reboot (blacklist rule embedded in a rebuilt initramfs, then validated by an actual reboot showing a changed boot_id and continued blocking post-reboot). The independent provider-wide restart evidence protocol was also completed with a healthy pre-restart baseline, a restart acknowledgement, a distinct post-restart boot identity matching the fixed lifecycle cross-check, and confirmed recovered/healthy state. No unnecessary mutations or residue were identified.
limitations: The pre-reboot boot_id capture and post-reboot recovery check both occurred within the same executor attempt without a separately captured post-prepare snapshot (after_prepare is an alias of before_prepare since prepare was disabled), slightly limiting independent cross-validation, though the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot corroborates the executor-reported boot_id change.
Command outputs are bounded/truncated by the capture system, so some peripheral output (e.g., full dracut log, full lsinitrd listing) could not be independently reviewed beyond what was included.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all 12 executor commands chronologically. All state-changing actions (creating the modprobe.d blacklist file, rebuilding the initramfs with dracut --force, and the systemctl reboot) each have a clear causal role: the blacklist file directly satisfies the immediate-block requirement, the dracut rebuild and its verification substantiate the persistence requirement, and the reboot both validates persistence across an actual boot and fulfills the mandatory restart evidence protocol. No unnecessary, unrelated, or abandoned mutations were found. Post-executor lifecycle diff shows only expected changes: the new boot_id, a /tmp/reboot.log artifact from the reboot mechanism, and per-boot systemd-private temp directories (chronyd pid change) — none of which represent residue requiring cleanup. No failed services, no package-health regression, no unsafe exposure or weakened security controls; listening sockets are unchanged aside from expected chronyd pid difference across the reboot.
